document.about: Thermo Scientific M Series centrifuges flyer (2 pages). The cover sets a 12 pt category tag in a red box above the 28 pt title, and the back page closes on a link line.

notes: 2026-11-24 (#122): a line ending in a web address, a domain, an e-mail address or a phone number was a heading when set bold or large.
2026-11-24 (#128): a kicker set in smaller type directly above the title opened an empty, deeper section ahead of it.

2026-11-24 (#112): the ordering table's shaded `IVD-MD | General Use Only` row has a rule under its first column only; the shading's edge is the line under the others, and the row and the first values below were read as one.

2026-11-25 (#195): the Specifications table, ruled with horizontals only, each row line broken at its column edges, ended after three rows: the page-wide reading took in the ordering table's rules too and found no columns, and the lines of a table ruled with horizontals only touch nothing. Its values set across both model columns were cut at the column edge, and every row was read as a section's band.

2026-11-25 (#195): the Application package table under it, ruled with horizontals only, broke its row lines at its columns as the Specifications table does, but no vertical stood on a break: its shaded header is drawn a column at a time, five fills meeting at the breaks. Its header and its two tall Everylab rows were loose text, and its six short rows a table read from text with the first of them for its header. A band of fills meeting end to end on every break states the columns as separators do.

checks.issue: The closing link line was a level-5 heading.
The 12pt category tag above the 28pt title was an empty level-5 section ahead of it.
#112: the header read `MT 17 / IVD-MD 75002576`, and the first row of values was lost into it.
#195: the table ended at `Max noise level`; the rest were headings and paragraphs.
#195: a value set across both model columns was cut at the column edge.
#195: the rows under the `Dimensions` band were lost, and each row of the table read as a band.
#195: the Everylab rows and the shaded header were loose text.
#195: the six short rows were a table of their own, its first row (`MT 17`) taken for the header.
